user_request: Build an AI document intelligence platform using AWS. It should allow users to upload PDF documents securely, extract text using OCR, identify PII, and store the metadata in a graph database for relationship querying.
normalized_request: Build a secure AI document intelligence platform that enables PDF upload, OCR-based text extraction, PII detection, and graph-based metadata storage for relationship queries.
domain: Document Intelligence / AI-Powered Data Extraction & Security

requirements.description: Users must securely upload PDF documents with authentication and authorization controls
Extract text content from PDF documents using OCR capabilities
Detect and identify personally identifiable information (PII) within extracted text
Store document metadata and detected entities in a queryable graph structure
Enable relationship-based querying across stored documents and entities
Enforce encryption for data at rest and in transit
Provide user-facing interface for document upload, viewing results, and executing queries
Track system performance, errors, and audit logs for compliance

components.name: SECURE_FILE_UPLOAD_AND_STORAGE
components.description: Manages secure PDF file ingestion, validation, encryption, and persistent storage with access controls

components.name: OCR_TEXT_EXTRACTION
components.description: Extracts text content from PDF documents using optical character recognition to convert images and scanned documents to machine-readable text

components.name: PII_DETECTION_AND_CLASSIFICATION
components.description: Identifies and classifies personally identifiable information (names, SSNs, emails, etc.) within extracted document text using AI models

components.name: GRAPH_DATABASE_STORAGE
components.description: Stores document metadata, extracted entities, and their relationships in a graph structure to enable entity relationship querying and traversal

components.name: RELATIONSHIP_QUERY_ENGINE
components.description: Executes graph queries to retrieve and traverse entity relationships, connections, and patterns across multiple documents

components.name: DOCUMENT_PROCESSING_ORCHESTRATOR
components.description: Coordinates the workflow between file upload, OCR extraction, PII detection, and graph storage with error handling and retry logic

components.name: USER_AUTHENTICATION_AND_AUTHORIZATION
components.description: Manages user identity verification, session management, role-based access control, and API authentication

components.name: DATA_ENCRYPTION_AND_KEY_MANAGEMENT
components.description: Enforces encryption for data at rest and in transit, manages cryptographic keys, and handles secure credential storage

components.name: WEB_USER_INTERFACE
components.description: Provides frontend interface for document upload, result viewing, PII alerts, and graph-based relationship queries

components.name: AUDIT_LOGGING_AND_MONITORING

risks: HIGH: PII Detection Model Accuracy - Custom-built PII detection may have false-negatives (missed sensitive data) or false-positives (over-aggressive redaction), creating compliance/security risks. Mitigation: Start with conservative high-confidence thresholds; establish feedback loop for continuous model improvement; conduct regular accuracy audits against labeled test sets.

HIGH: Graph Database Performance at Scale - Complex relationship queries on large document corpora (10M+ entities) may exhibit slow performance, causing user experience degradation. Mitigation: Implement comprehensive indexing strategy; design schema to minimize traversal depth; conduct early performance testing; implement query timeouts and result limits.

HIGH: Encryption Key Management Operational Burden - CipherTrust introduces operational complexity (key rotation, backup/recovery, high-availability); failures could make data unrecoverable. Mitigation: Establish clear operational procedures; automate key rotation; implement multiple redundancy levels; conduct disaster recovery drills.

MEDIUM: OCR Accuracy Variability - Tesseract OCR accuracy varies significantly by document quality (scanned PDFs, poor resolution, non-standard fonts). Low accuracy reduces downstream PII detection effectiveness. Mitigation: Implement image preprocessing (deskewing, denoising); set confidence thresholds for extracted text; provide manual review/correction capability.

MEDIUM: Third-Party Dependency Management - Reliance on open-source libraries (Tesseract, spaCy, Presidio) and third-party services (AWS, CipherTrust) creates vulnerability to library vulnerabilities, API changes, or service outages. Mitigation: Establish dependency monitoring; implement security scanning in CI/CD; maintain version compatibility matrix; have fallback strategies.

MEDIUM: Graph Query Complexity & Authorization - Relationship queries could expose unintended data through complex traversals; ensuring row-level security across all query patterns is challenging. Mitigation: Implement query validation/sanitization; restrict query syntax to prevent full-graph scans; audit all query results for authorization compliance.

MEDIUM: Scalability of Asynchronous Processing - Document processing pipeline (OCR, PII detection) must handle variable load; queue overflow or slow processing could create service degradation. Mitigation: Implement auto-scaling; set queue depth limits; prioritize processing queues; implement graceful degradation (failed items to dead-letter queue).

MEDIUM: Data Privacy Compliance - Handling PII-containing documents requires strict compliance with GDPR, CCPA, state privacy laws; non-compliance creates legal liability. Mitigation: Implement data retention/deletion policies; maintain audit trails; provide data export/deletion APIs; conduct privacy impact assessments.

LOW: StoreX Project Maintenance Status - No GitHub metrics provided; if project is unmaintained, security vulnerabilities could go unfixed. Mitigation: Verify GitHub activity before adoption; fork if necessary; establish plan to maintain/patch if needed.

LOW: Streamlit Production Readiness - Streamlit designed for data apps/dashboards; may lack enterprise features (fine-grained security, audit logging, accessibility). Mitigation: Supplement with custom components for production requirements; conduct security hardening; implement accessibility testing.

LOW: Integration Complexity Between Components - Coordinate 10 components across backend/frontend; integration mismatches could cause workflow failures. Mitigation: Establish clear API contracts; implement comprehensive integration testing; use event-driven architecture for loose coupling.
assumptions: AWS Environment Available: Assumes AWS account with sufficient IAM permissions, networking, and service quota allowances (S3, RDS/Neptune, Lambda, SQS, CloudWatch, etc.). If using alternative cloud provider, adaptation required.

Graph Database Selection: Assumes Neo4j or Amazon Neptune will be selected for COMP-004. If alternative graph database chosen (e.g., ArangoDB, JanusGraph), query language and integration patterns may differ.

OCR Accuracy Acceptable: Assumes Tesseract OCR provides acceptable accuracy for document types in scope (business documents, legal documents, forms). High-accuracy requirements (e.g., medical records with specialized terminology) may require premium OCR services (AWS Textract, Google Cloud Vision, Azure Computer Vision).

PII Detection Library Availability: Assumes open-source PII detection libraries (Microsoft Presidio, spaCy NER, regex patterns) provide sufficient accuracy for PII detection requirements. Highly specialized PII types or domain-specific entities may require custom model training.

Encryption Key Management Overhead Acceptable: Assumes operational overhead of CipherTrust key management is justified by security/compliance requirements. Simpler organizations may use AWS KMS directly without separate key management platform.
Multi-Tenancy Required: Assumes platform serves multiple organizations/users with data isolation requirements. Single-tenant deployments could simplify authorization logic.

Batch Processing Model: Assumes document processing is batch-oriented (users upload documents, wait for async processing, then query results). Real-time streaming processing would require significant architecture changes.

Audit Logging Retention Period: Assumes 7-year audit log retention requirement (typical for financial/healthcare compliance). Different industries have different retention requirements; adjust log retention policies accordingly.

User-Facing Query Complexity: Assumes end-users can construct graph queries via UI query builder with simplified abstraction over Cypher/AQL. If users require full query language expressiveness, steeper learning curve expected.

StoreX, instaread-backend, CipherTrust Project Maturity: Assumes selected candidates are sufficiently mature and actively maintained. Verify GitHub repository stats, license types, and security audit history before final adoption.

FastAPI/Spring Boot Ecosystem Compatibility: Assumes FastAPI backend (COMP-002, COMP-006) and Spring Boot backend (COMP-001) can interoperate via REST APIs and share infrastructure (Kubernetes, monitoring, encryption keys). Alternative deployment models (serverless, separate infrastructure) may complicate integration.

Compliance Requirements in Scope: Assumes GDPR, CCPA, and SOC 2 compliance requirements are in scope. Additional compliance (HIPAA, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP) would require additional security controls not explicitly detailed.
